entries.lore: Anciuxor's primary manifestation domain is REALM I (the universe · mortal-substrate worlds and cosmic space).

Ultharis cannot enter Realm I or Realm II · but he OBSERVES REALM II (the Immortalands · where Immortals govern the afterlife of dead mortal souls in Virtua/Infernia sectors) to assess HOW WELL EACH IMMORTAL IS DOING THEIR JOB.
Abominalys, 'The Endless Catastrophe' — Guardian of Existential Failure, and the final failsafe of the Expanse.

Abyssion, 'The Dimensional Maw' — Guardian of Collapse. Where Alphaea creates order, Abyssion governs destruction: he consumes unstable dimensions before their corruption can spread across the Expanse, devouring broken realities, failed timelines, dimensional infections and…

Aetherion, 'The Prism Tyrant' — Guardian of Evolution. He governs adaptation, mutation, astralite evolution, cosmic transformation and infinite growth, embodying the law that existence must continuously evolve to survive.

Aethravax, 'The Twin Dominion' — Guardian of Cosmic Polarity, and the rarest and most mysterious of the six. He governs duality, balance through opposition, simultaneous creation and destruction, astralite polarity and cosmic judgment.
Alphaea, 'The First Radiance' — Guardian of Divine Order. An original Dracolord forged by the Aenor Eruption among the 1000+ primordial dragons, and one of only six to survive the great dying.
Azyrath, 'The Hollow Empress' — Guardian of the Void. She governs emptiness, silence, gravity, cosmic hollowness and suspended existence.

Ovauron, 'The Wandering Hunger' — designation AE-28. The Anomaly of the Dichotomy Zone (Q2) of the Aethryx Expanse: a sentient 'drift planet,' a null world that carries no reality weight, adrift outside the cosmic order.

Aionis does not measure time — he governs it through pure control. Every moment in Viridia flows through his will. To face Aionis is to age before you strike, leaving behind nothing but memory of the past.

Ambrevon embodies perfection, where form and power reach their peak. It exists as the standard all life unconsciously strives toward. Bound to the core, it drives evolution through dominance and inevitability.

Azurel the Sapphirelord is a higher intelligence beyond physical form, processing Zyraxis as a system rather than a world. It influences expansion, knowledge, and cosmic awareness. Even bound, its calculations ripple through advanced beings and alien structures.

[★ THE ELDER PRIME OF NEXYROS · THE MYRACLESE HUMANOID PRIME · COSMIC ORIGIN OF ALL HUMANOID POPULATIONS ACROSS THE AETHRYX EXPANSE · PEAK Bk I LORE] The Elder Prime — also called the MYRACLESE HUMANOID PRIME — is the cosmic origin figure who spawned HUMANOID POPULATIONS ACROSS…

Emeralix, the Emerabord, is a living ecosystem, embodying growth, balance, and the persistence of life. Forests, oceans, and creatures all trace their origin to its influence. Bound to the core, it ensures life continues even in a fractured system.
Eurakeon was born from ruin — the shadow aura that Anciuxor purged from Omegoran (the corruption of Elzoran) did not die.
v9.6 CANON ESCALATION: Excidior's Bk VI Dragonsong Castle Fall action is upgraded from 'destroys castle + takes corrupted Onyxaxus the Onyxwyngg' to the FULL DYNASTY-WIPE EVENT.

v9.7.1 REFINEMENT (SUPERSEDES v9.7.0 reframe · CORRECTS to canonical position): IMPERION IS A VICE IMMORTAL OF VIRIDIA (Immortalitia class). He is NOT classified outside the Vice/Virtue divide — he is canonically Vice-aligned.

Ivirium, the Pearlord, is the mediator of the Gemlords, embodying order, balance, and divine structure. It was entrusted by Oathane to maintain harmony between all forces. Bound within Corefall, its absence leaves the system without true neutrality.

v9.6 COSMIC PILLAR INHERITANCE LOCK: BLUES + YELLOWS predominantly inherited KALENATEL'S Wizard-Astrum pillar (LIGHT · wisdom · refined-cosmic substrate). REDS + GREENS predominantly inherited MYKARLYTH'S Greatkin pillar (MASS · instinct · grounded-physical substrate).

Virtue Immortal of Humankind — among the oldest active immortal-class beings in Viridian history. The Highest One entrusted him with the Covenant of Humanity: protect their potential, not their choices.

Virtue Immortal of Wonder — a primordial being of pure astral energy, and the oldest counterpart to Imperion (Dominion). Vice-pair: Mira ⟷ Imperion = wonder vs. control, one of the cosmos's oldest philosophical fractures.

Mutaryn, the Citrinelord, represents evolution in its purest form, constantly adapting and mutating to survive any condition. Its presence accelerates change across all creature life. Even in containment, it drives instability and rapid transformation.

v9.6 COSMIC PILLAR INHERITANCE LOCK: REDS + GREENS predominantly inherited MYKARLYTH'S Greatkin pillar (MASS · instinct · grounded-physical substrate). BLUES + YELLOWS predominantly inherited KALENATEL'S Wizard-Astrum pillar (LIGHT · wisdom · refined-cosmic substrate).
Virtue Immortal of Nature — Mother Nature, who established every living system in Viridia and the ecological balance that holds them together.

Ninth of the Ten, and not risen as the first eight were, Oathane embodies pure calculation and enforced equilibrium. It governs structure, correction, and the logic that binds existence together. Where imbalance emerges, Oathane restores order without mercy or bias.

Tenth of the Ten, sharing the Ninth's guarded origin, Oatheus embodies will, creation, and divine authority. It shapes reality through intent, commanding the flow of existence itself. Where purpose rises, Oatheus defines what all things are meant to become.

When the higher Gemlords vanished, Obsidius did not mourn — it acted. It bound the remaining lords in place, locking the world from collapse. The last enforcer standing — the fragile line between order and oblivion.

Vice Immortal of Hatred — a primordial being of pure astral energy, and the embodiment of hatred and division across Viridia. Vice-pair of the Virtue Immortal Aionis (Time): where Aionis orders cause and effect, Odion is the resentment that festers in the spaces between.

The Crimson One is the origin of all predatory instinct and the force that drives dominance across the Beastlands, shaping survival through violence and territorial rule. It does not govern or command — it exists as the undeniable truth that strength alone decides who remains.

Vice Immortal of Lust — a primordial being of pure astral energy. Vice-pair of the Virtue Immortal Amora (Love/Beauty): Theia is desire with the devotion stripped out, want that has lost the will to give. Governs the domain of Lust across Viridia.

Vaelorith — Vice Immortal of GREED (1 of 24 Immortals · all Tier VIII per v8.9 standardization). Pre-Bk-V canonical location: VAULT OF THE COMPROMISED at Khronexus · holds Malviros's bound soul among others.

Primordialis Custodis. Formed in regions where Aetheon influence stabilized extreme Astral concentrations. Armored constructs of stone and metal sustained by internal energy. Singular purpose: defend and maintain structured environments. Unwavering discipline.

Imperion is canonically a VICE IMMORTAL of Viridia (Immortalitia class) · NOT outside the Vice/Virtue divide. His Dominion-pillar gives him the cosmic-sovereign capacity to rule the Immortalands · but his classification is Vice.
Andre Hart — 2020 CE Central region · age 25 · THE FINAL ENTRY of the codex per v9.0. Andre represents THE BRIDGE BETWEEN ORDINARY LIFE AND COSMIC TRUTH.

Primordialis Ruinis. Emerged from regions of intense geothermal pressure where Astral energy accumulated beyond stability. Charred exterior, molten interior — heat releases through cracks in their form. Move in unstable, convulsive patterns; gather to release built-up energy.
Egnellahc, Humanoid Prime — the first humanoid and the origin of all humanoid life across the Aethryx Expanse.

Aetheon of Spirit. Emerged where Astral energy pooled most densely, influenced by consciousness and inner balance. Bridges thought, soul, and existence — does not act, connects. Established spirit as the inner essence separating consciousness from physical form.

Elyssia Eldersoul — the first divine humanoid and origin of all human life in Viridia. Conceived through the union of Lucienis and Theia, carrying both the impulse of desire and the capacity for creation.

Primordialis Luminis. Emerged spontaneously from the perfect ecosystem of the Eastern forests, formed from pure astral energy. Small luminous humanoids with delicate wings; channel natural and light energy. Speak Olden — the first language. Harmonious, communal.

Primordialis Dominus. The final stage of primordial beast evolution — instinct transforms into absolute dominance. Do not hunt traditionally — they establish control over entire regions, forcing all life to submit or adapt. Their presence reshapes ecological hierarchies.

Aetheon of Ice. Formed where stillness overtook motion — Concordia's peace and Despera's sorrow froze regions into silence. Does not attack — halts. Established preservation through stillness, slowing decay and protecting what must remain. Leans Virtue (Concordia dominance).

Primordialis Ascendis. Emerged when clusters of Faes converged under sustained Virtue-Immortal influence, forming singular advanced entities. Tall radiant humanoids of condensed light. Guide lesser beings through intuition; stabilize regions, promote harmony.

Aetheon of Shadow. Established shadow as the counterforce to light, allowing concealment, depth, and the unseen. Created spaces where form is hidden and perception is limited. Born of Mortis + Invidia (absence + envy, Vice). Domain: Sleep cycle / Dream realm.
Omegoran is Elzoran corrupted — the apex dragon after a shadow aura consumed him, fracturing his body beyond natural evolution into a catastrophic Unknown-class entity drifting between dimensions.

Primordialis Voxis. Developed from advanced Whisper networks granted autonomy through prolonged Immortal interaction. Semi-humanoid layered forms existing between perception and reality. Transmit thought, memory, intent — speak in impressions, not language.

NAMING DISAMBIGUATION (canonical): The Water Aetheon is officially OULIRIS — the cosmic-being class · Tier VII · Water/Spirit substrate. The mortal Naturism Founder is OULIRA AQUARIS (# 172 · Tier IV Legend · Eastern religious leader).

Aetheon of Fire. Born from the violent pressure of Viridia's core as Immortal conflict intensified heat. Does not simply burn — seeks release. Established fire as the force of transformation, breaking matter down and remaking it. Born of Excidior + Heraya (Vice).

Primordialis Feralis. Originated when a Whisper was forced into physical form by Stultor — created the first hybrid humanoid through mischief, not design. Small horned humanoids with animalistic traits, unstable spirit + creature features. Chaotic but not inherently malicious.

Aetheon of Light. Established light as the force of illumination, allowing reality to be seen, revealed, and understood. Born of Fidesio + Mira (faith + inspiration, Virtue). Domain: the Daytime (Sun).

Primordialis Sylvarum. Formed through Fae resonance with the forest. Tall beings with bark-like skin, vine-grown features, antler-like extensions. Manipulate growth and terrain; stabilize ecosystems. Calm and rooted. Worldsense: Force / Ground / Spirit.

Aetheon of Ground. Emerged from the slow, deliberate movement of land as Natura and Aldoris imposed order and longevity upon the earth. Does not destroy — endures. Established ground as the foundation of existence. Pure stability pairing (Virtue).

Aetheon of Force. Formed under the immense pressure of domination, where force itself became concentrated. Established force as a governing constant — anchoring strength into the fabric of reality, making movement, collision, and pressure unavoidable laws.

Primordialis Terranis. Emerged when ancient Sylvans accumulated centuries of environmental resonance, evolving into singular embodiments of entire ecosystems. Massive forms of stone, root, and living forest — shape terrain by presence alone.

Primordialis Maledicta. Formed when balanced ecosystems collapsed under prolonged corruption, twisting natural life into predatory self-sustaining entities. Elongated asymmetrical forms blend organic and parasitic traits; spread corruption through contact.

Aetheon of Tech. Formed as the land organized itself into patterns of logic and structure. A being of living circuitry — not creating technology but BEING technology in its purest form. Established progression through systems, enabling intelligence to evolve into tools.

Primordialis Oldneris. Created by the Immortals as living conduits for communication across the forests. Floating spheres of light with unseen humanoid silhouettes; true forms exist just beyond physical perception.

Henry Hart — son of DANIEL HART (the migrator · Gen 6 · per v9.6 Daniel card lock). Born ~1930s CE in the Centralands during the Falling Skies Era. The FIRST FULL-SUBURBAN HART — Daniel migrated the family back to the Centralands but raised Henry as ordinary Centralands citizen.

Hymynos Crosswind VI — 205 CE Central · united rival Central districts through diplomacy · formed the Crosswinds Pact based on shared interest. Negotiated balance between competing powers · created rare period of cooperation. Achieved unity without domination.

Ignycel circles the broken peaks where fire, frost, and storm refuse to settle their old argument. Its wings carry the cold the mountain forgot, its crown carries the flame the mountain remembers, and the lightning trailing behind it is the argument itself, still unresolved.
Jetron rose out of a scrapyard floating in the deep dark, built piece by piece from the leavings of fleets no one came back to claim.

Juno Halcyon — Super Period aligned hero · VPS A1 licensed (per Provost Lyle Meridian's 1925 CE astral licensing logic per v9.3) · specialized in exposing illusion-based infiltrations. Counterpart to Sable Rowan's Mori-mimic unmasking work. VPS A1 Champion.

Kaedryn Frostpoint — 292 CE Northern figure who broke from the Northern Crown's authority · claimed Frostpoint Peak as independent stronghold. Believed centralized control could no longer protect region's interests.

Kael Redbanner — 176 CE Western figure who unified western warbands under the Redveil Empire. Launched coordinated campaigns to seize and hold new territories. Raised the Redbanner as symbol of permanent claim. Replaced roaming survival with sustained expansion.

Korven Highreach — 168 CE Western · led continuous Great Canyon campaigns. Made constant warfare the defining condition of Western life. Survival depended on proven ability. Delayed unity. Solidified Western identity as combat-driven.

Krovyn — Super Period morally-gray operator predating the Supernova Era · VPS A1 licensed but interpreting OVV doctrine to deny rather than protect. Foundational case for the 'doctrine over life' Super Period anti-pattern. VPS A1 Champion.
Legarion Oldsoul — 166 CE Southern · crushed rival clans through overwhelming force · burned settlements to prevent resistance · ruled through fear. Normalized violence as governance.
Lyssara Iceveil — 285 CE Northern figure who expanded the Iceveil Dynasty through strategic marriages · absorbed rival bloodlines into her own to consolidate power without open war.

Margaret Hart — daughter of HENRY HART (Gen 7 · per v9.6). Born ~1950s CE in the Centralands suburbs · the Stormvale Period adjacent generation (Carl Stormvale II takes Black Thunder Allegiance lead 1968 CE per v9.3 during her adult years).

Marris Venn — 200 CE Eastern figure who formalized the Tidemarsh Swamp into Eastern power. Reduced piracy · restored stability to trade · safe passage across Oceania and Glasscurrent Bay routes. Transformed isolated naval efforts into unified system of cooperation.

Mealux drifts through sanctums no mortal hand carved, a key that has forgotten which door it was made for. Its pink iris holds a single red heart at its center, and the galaxies set around the frame turn slowly — each one a lock somewhere across the Expanse.
Mutamech crash-landed somewhere a long way from home and walked the rest of the way in the suit that broke its fall.

Oshen Koi — Super Period morally-gray operator · VPS A1 licensed but corruptly monetizing hero contracts. Foundational case for OVV procurement scandal investigations of mid-Modernization Era. VPS A1 Champion.
King Pelagus Finn — 333 CE Central Heartplains figure · rose as the Royal Educator · one of the foremost intellectual figures during early stages of the First War.

King Raegis Redrock — 341 CE Western figure of Redrock Run · seized control · established tyrannical regime built on internal oppression and absolute authority. Enforced strict control over his people using fear and punishment to maintain order within his domain.

Ragnar Whitefang — 173 CE Northern figure who united scattered tundra tribes under the Whitefang Pact to resist southern raids. Forged coalition based on mutual defense. Transitioned North from isolated survival to organized alliance.

Ragnor Thunderstep — 203 CE Western figure who unified Western territories through relentless campaigns + overwhelming force + uncompromising dominance. Established absolute rule. Unity through fear · not shared purpose. Suppressed opposition · failed to create lasting loyalty.

Sable Rowan — Super Period aligned hero · VPS A1 licensed · specialized in publicly unmasking Mori mimics during Supernova-Era infiltration scares. Counterpart to Juno Halcyon's illusion-exposure work. VPS A1 Champion.

King Serren Atlas — 334 CE Central Atlas Junction ruler during the First War years. Continued the Atlas line (Solvar Atlas 188 CE · Elyndra Atlas 269 CE) through the early Blood War period · maintained the trade-route control that made the Central Region the economic gateway of…

Sharkfin dominates the battlefield with a predator's instinct and a warmachine's precision. Its infrared beam sears through nearly all matter, while its jaws and tail unleash relentless destruction and storm-born chaos.

This ancient entity exists beyond fixed form, its body reshaping with each passing moment. The glowing sigils carved into its frame are said to whisper a forgotten language — one that twists reality itself.

Skybeam is a hybrid predator of beast and machine, engineered for aerial dominance and precision strikes. Its laser vision allows it to track and eliminate targets from a distance while its claws deliver devastating close-range damage.
Snok emerged from the deepest part of the moss-forest where the carnivorous flowers had been quietly practicing.

Solvar Atlas — 188 CE Central figure who founded the Atlas Dominion · secured control over major trade routes crossing the Central Region. Organized movement · taxation · passage through regulated system. Central Region became economic gateway of Viridia.

Thalric Glacierborne — 186 CE Northern figure who consolidated power over the Frozen Lakes through strict control of food · routes · winter stores. Governed through unyielding policies. Refused to adapt as conditions worsened.

Titanova crawls across forgotten wastelands, older than the ruins it walks among. The civilizations that built it left no record of its purpose, only relics scattered in its wake — keyboards, towers, machines no one remembers using.

Vaeldrik Crownice — 208 CE Northern figure who united fractured Northern clans under a single frozen banner · established Crown of Ice as first true Northern superpower. Enforced discipline and expansion. Achieved unprecedented strength and territorial control.

Vaerys Silverstone — 314 CE Central figure ruling Silverstone Heights · the wealthiest stronghold in Viridia · securing immense resources and economic influence. Domain became prime target for early Western rebels seeking to disrupt Central dominance.
Veylith does not enter battle — it appears where it is least expected. Existing as a drifting consciousness, it hides within crowded places, slipping between bodies until it finds one worth taking.
Veyron Glacius II — 300 CE Northern figure (Pre-Blood War era begins) · led reclamation of Frostpoint Peak following its brief independence under Kaedryn · restored it to Northern Crown authority.

Voidward is what Steelward becomes when the gate finally falls and the oath has no one left to keep. It returned without permission, hauling itself from a sarcophagus no one had bothered to seal, missing one eye and carrying something else behind the other.

Volcarith was born at the seam where the lava-fields meet the night tide, a contradiction the world has not figured out how to resolve. Its body holds the ocean and its spine holds the eruption, and neither has been able to extinguish the other.

Xytabyte is a precision-engineered predator, combining mechanical warfare systems with biological lethality. Its explosive web cannons control space and slow its targets, while its venom ensures they weaken with every passing moment.

Zarakai is what Sprinklez found, in the velvet-room at the palace, when no one was looking. The horn fell, the wings dispersed, and something else took up residence behind the still-familiar face — patient, armored, and very polite about the sword.

Abyssiq surfaces from trenches that do not appear on any star-chart, wearing armor stitched together from things it found at the bottom. The twin cores set into its chest pulse with the rhythm of a sea it has long since left behind.

Buzzolt drifts above ruined shrines no one bothers to repair, drawn to the runes that still hum after a thousand years. Its wings carry small storms in their patterns, and each flicker of lightning is the shrine itself agreeing to be remembered.
Chronocrow was a clocktower before it was anything else, lowered onto cable-legs by hands that did not understand what they had built.

Dredgill prowls the kelp-trenches with a mouth that arrived before the rest of its body did. Its teeth grew first, its hunger second, its frame somewhere afterward and never quite caught up. Smaller fish do not flee it; they freeze, which is what it counts on.

This winter-born spirit rises not from flame, but from silence and snow. Where others burn to ash, it freezes, preserving itself in cycles of cold rebirth. Its wings carry storms, and its cry stills the air itself — turning even the fiercest battles into frozen echoes.

Gearbyte is a reinforced combat unit built from early prototypes designed for direct engagement and heavy impact. Its extended arms allow it to strike from a distance while maintaining pressure on its target. Once it closes the gap, it overwhelms through force.

Glaciogre crawls down from the ice ridges with an axe heavier than its body and a temper smaller than its bite. Its patchwork armor was stitched by no one in particular, repaired by the cold itself when nothing else would.

Gravemite drifts the dustbowls where no one buries the dead because no one remembers them well enough. The eyes did not belong to it once — they were found, kept, and slowly forgotten how to put down.
Gravemourn is what Gravemite becomes when the forgetting catches up to it. The cloth no longer rises — it sits, heavy, smoldering from beneath, the loss that never resolved finally finding fuel.

Once a farmbound creature, Grimhog was twisted by a force that turned instinct into rage and flesh into something far more dangerous. It roams graveyards and abandoned lands, drawn to decay and conflict, its body burning with a fire it cannot control.
This playful trickster dances through the night with a grin and a spark of chaos. Armed with flame-tipped arrows and restless energy, it turns every encounter into a game of unpredictability.

Levanium drifts the trenches where light has not been a memory for centuries, the dome above its eyes pulsing a slow blue rhythm the coral has learned to fear. Its tentacles do not hunt; they wait, while the brain decides what is worth reaching for.
Neuromoo was harvested somewhere off-world and rebuilt by hands that had never seen the animal it used to be.

This mischievous shadow lurks where light fades and silence grows thick. It drifts unseen through the night, its grin the only warning before reality begins to slip. Those who encounter it are often left questioning what was real — and what it chose to let them remember.

Riftipple darts between worlds the way other creatures dart between branches, dragging a thumbnail-sized galaxy behind its ears like a halo. The tear above its head is not a wound but a door, one it does not seem to remember opening or closing.

Rustbytes are early-stage robotic units built for basic support and field assistance. Though limited in power, they adapt quickly and enhance nearby allies during combat. They become extremely valuable when supporting stronger units.

Saburrow runs the ruin-fields at dusk, its body shaped from the desert itself and held together by something close to memory. When it stops, it forgets it is alive; when it moves, the sand remembers being a fox.

A scavenger of the Wastelands, Raxeen survives by finding value where others see nothing. He strikes fast, adapts faster, and disappears before retaliation can land. In a world built on power, Scrapjaw thrives on opportunity.

Smogrim slips through ruins that were not ruined when it last visited, leaving a wake of dark vapor and the smell of charged air. The red lightning above its wings is older than anything it has met on this world, and its laugh is the only language it has bothered to learn.

Spargus walks into the gym like he was born under the ropes, the mushroom cap above his face and the fungal weight at his fists earned in fights no one trained him for. He does not remember which came first — the fighting or the fungus — and the corner-men do not ask.

Sprinklez was found in the tapestry-room of a palace no one had visited for years, curled on a chair as if she had always belonged there. The horn and the wings appeared overnight, the way certain dreams appear overnight, and the staff agreed quietly never to mention either.

Steelward holds the gate it was sworn to and has held it long past anyone who remembers the oath. Inside its helm there is only red light and the slow rhythm of duty, undisturbed by the centuries piling up on its pauldrons.

Terralith has crossed the same canyon so many times it no longer notices the canyon — it notices the canyon noticing it. Its shell carries the strata of every age it has walked through, pressed in like calendar pages no one can read.

Vampella moves through twilight as if the hour itself were her ally. She does not chase — she invites. Those who meet her eyes describe a cold elegance, a hunger framed as conversation; by the time the bargain has been struck, no one who has met her remembers the same way twice.

Veridrax was not born in the wild but in the seams of older walls, where a single gem of unknown origin pressed itself into the egg before it hatched. The crystal grew where its heart should have, and the dragon grew around it, never quite sure which one was carrying the other.
Wynwyrm drifts where suffering gathers, neither hunting nor hiding. Its presence is the first relief — the moment a wound begins to close, the moment a fearful breath finally slows.
